editorial:
Imagine being the sibling who always felt second best. That is exactly where you find Iris. While her sister Rose is married, pregnant, and clearly the favorite child, Iris is just trying to find her place. When their mother passes away, it does not bring the sisters closer. Instead, it pushes Iris over the edge. You get to see her world fall apart as she tries to deal with her grief and her feelings of being left behind. The whole movie feels heavy and raw, like you are watching someone truly lose their grip on reality while trying to numb the pain.

The acting is what really sells the story, as you can feel Iris's pain in every scene. Some parts move a bit slow, but that just helps you feel how stuck she is in her own head. If you like stories about family secrets and messy emotions, you will love this. You should definitely look for a 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection for the best picture. If you are in a hurry, renting it on Apple TV is a great way to catch it tonight without spending too much money.
endingExplained: In the end, Iris finally reaches a breaking point where she can no longer run from her sadness. After a series of wild and self-destructive choices, she has a final confrontation with Rose. You see her realize that her mother's love was complicated and unfair. She stops trying to hide in her bad habits and starts to accept the truth about her family. The movie ends with her finally starting to heal and find some peace.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves deep stories about family conflict and healing.
